title: Direct Cultivation of Entangled $|CS\rangle$ Magic States
abstract: Magic-state cultivation has so far focused mainly on single-qubit non-Clifford resources. We develop a direct cultivation architecture for the entangled state $|CS\rangle=CS|++\rangle$. Two commuting Clifford involutions project onto four usable branches related by Pauli-frame updates. A minimal six-bit $[6,2,4]$ record protects the branch label against readout errors that map one valid record to another. Verified CAT$_7$ gadgets, Steane error detection, CZZ-based controlled checks, and immediate Steane-to-surface expansion form the complete factory. The decoder uses 263 operational detector bits, while 168 additional bits are withheld for later validation. Decoding proceeds through exact low-order resolution, a precomputed higher-order catalogue, and four-coset BP+OSD. Under the stated active-location stochastic-Pauli model, exact enumeration finds no accepted closed-boundary logical-failure mechanism through fault order two, while explicit order-three failure mechanisms exist. Finite-$p$ simulations quantify acceptance, residual syndromes, and decoder workload, and targeted sampling of order-three faults estimates the leading logical-error channels. Optimizing the direct $d=5\rightarrow13$ expansion reduces accepted-output operation count by approximately 35--37\%. We compare the two routes at the same binary logical-error rate. Direct CS remains cheaper in operation count at the two lower-noise benchmark points even when the three-$T$ route is given pre-existing output patches. The ordering reverses between $8\times10^{-4}$ and $9\times10^{-4}$. These results show that an entangled non-Clifford state can be cultivated directly with a protected branch record and an explicitly certified fault-order-three output channel.
summary: This paper details a novel, fault-tolerant architecture for directly generating the entangled magic state $|CSangle$ required for quantum computation. By employing a protected branch record and advanced error correction gadgets, the authors demonstrate that this direct method can be significantly more resource-efficient than established indirect preparation methods at low noise levels. This advances the practical feasibility assessment of fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of developing a direct, fault-tolerant quantum circuit architecture for cultivating the entangled non-Clifford magic state $|CSangle$. It aims to compare this direct method against established indirect resource preparation routes.
main_result: The direct cultivation route was shown to be operationally cheaper than the three-T route at two lower-noise benchmark points, demonstrating a viable, fault-tolerant method for generating the required non-Clifford resource.
method: The authors employed detailed quantum error correction analysis, including the use of a minimal six-check classical record, verified CAT7 gadgets, and advanced decoding algorithms like four-coset BP+OSD.
model_or_system: The work is situated in the context of fault-tolerant quantum computation, specifically utilizing Steane error detection and expanding from smaller surface code patches ($d=5$) to larger ones ($d=13$).
key_observables: Operation count (active locations), Logical Error Rate (LER), and the fault order of the certified output channel (order three).
important_parameters: Physical error rate ($p$), logical error rate ($L_g(p)$), and the required resource overhead (e.g., 263 detector bits).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed under the active-location stochastic-Pauli model, and comparisons often rely on assumptions regarding pre-existing output patches for the indirect route.
figures_summary: Figures compare the resource costs (active locations) and logical error rates between the direct cultivation route and the indirect three-T route across varying noise levels.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the target state and its projection, detailing the error protection mechanism using a six-check record, presenting the full factory architecture, and concluding with a quantitative comparison of resource costs and error performance against the standard indirect method.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, resource-cost analysis for generating a crucial non-Clifford resource state, which is fundamental for universal quantum computation protocols.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Architecture overview and indirect comparator. (a) The indirect route prepares three logical |T⟩L resources and converts them to |CS⟩L with a Clifford+T circuit. (b) The direct route starts from two Steane [[7, 1, 3]] blocks in |+⟩L, applies the six-check sequence C1, C2, C12 | Dmid | C1, C2, C12, and immediately transfers the accepted state through the Steane-to-d = 5 escape and direct d = 5→13 surface-code growth. The three-T route is used only as a resource comparator.

FIG. 2. Six-check measurement sequence and coded record. (a) The two Steane blocks undergo C1, C2, and C12 measurements, midpoint error detection Dmid, and a second measurement triple. (b) The ideal history g6(a, b) = (a, b, a ⊕ b, a, b, a ⊕b) forms a [6, 2, 4] record code. (c) Records outside the four valid codewords are rejected. (d) All four ideal branches are usable and differ only by the Pauli-frame update Za AZb B.

FIG. 3. Steane-coordinate checks and CZZ-based compilation. (a) Matching coordinates of Steane blocks A and B realize the logical checks C1, C2, and C12 through transversal products of the local operators. (b) A cat ancilla controls G∗= C(H ⊗H), synthesized from one CZZ interaction and local Ry(π/4) rotations. Clifford wrappers Q1, Q2, and Q12 give the three coordinate checks. The six-check core contains 42 CZZ, 56 CX, and 224 one-qubit locations.

FIG. 4. Factory yield and accepted-output classification. (a) Acceptance of the six-check core and the complete factory. The two curves use independent calibration and evaluation samples. (b) Sources of rejection before the downstream stage. (c) Number of sampled fault locations in operationally accepted runs. (d) Accepted outputs are classified as either closed at the validation boundary or containing a detectable residual syndrome. Detectable residuals are not retrospectively rejected.

Figure 5(b) shows how decoder workload changes with p. The fraction of nontrivial records that reach the four- coset BP+OSD stage grows from about 4.7% at 10−4 to 44.7% at 10−3, while the median gap falls from 13.24 to 6.91. Every audited record has full four-coset coverage and no BP+OSD decoding failure is observed. The trend therefore reflects increasing ambiguity at higher p.
